profile.reading:
TierPoint's Allentown-TekPark data center occupies Building 4 of a nine-building, 508,000-square-foot technology campus at 9999 Hamilton Boulevard in Breinigsville, Pennsylvania, in Lehigh County near Allentown, on 137 acres with an unusually well-documented history reaching back to 1987, when the campus was originally built as an AT&T Bell Labs research site. Ownership passed through TriQuint Semiconductor, which acquired it from Agere Systems in 2003, then to Hamilton TEK Partners in 2005, before DBSi announced plans to develop part of the campus into data center space in 2011. Xand acquired DBSi's data center operations later that year, and TierPoint gained control of the TekPark facility in 2014 through its own acquisition of Xand, initially operating under a lease. On October 23, 2025, TierPoint outright purchased the TekPark real estate from its prior owner, MRA Group, funding the deal with a 240 million dollar asset-backed securitization, and simultaneously announced a 100-megawatt power expansion targeted for completion in the second half of 2026. The current data center building spans more than 122,000 total square feet with more than 96,000 square feet of raised floor and over 8,000 square feet of business-continuity seating, running at roughly 16 megawatts of current power capacity. The site holds SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II certifications including HITRUST, and is HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, ISO 27001, and ITAR compliant. TierPoint, headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, describes its national footprint as roughly 40 data centers across 20 US markets. As is standard industry practice, tenant identities are not publicly disclosed, and no specific Uptime Institute Tier level is stated for this building.

TierPoint has also grown through significant recent capital raises beyond its acquisition history: a 320 million dollar equity round in April 2020 led by Argo Infrastructure Partners, Wafra, and Macquarie Capital Principal Finance alongside existing investors, followed by Argo's 500 million dollar investment in February 2022 that made it TierPoint's largest single equity investor, and a further increase to Argo's ownership and capital commitment announced in December 2025.
profile.research_note: Rich, well-documented ownership history via Data Center Dynamics (Oct 2025): campus built 1987 as an AT&T Bell Labs site, TriQuint Semiconductor acquired from Agere Systems 2003, Hamilton TEK Partners bought the campus 2005, DBSi announced data center plans 2011, Xand acquired DBSi's data center operations 2011, TierPoint gained control of TekPark in 2014 via its acquisition of Xand. TierPoint leased the site for years, then outright purchased the real estate from prior owner MRA Group on Oct 23, 2025, funded by a $240M asset-backed securitization, with a 100MW power expansion targeted for completion H2 2026. This is one of TierPoint's most substantively documented acquisition histories of any facility researched this session. Ownership correction: TierPoint is not majority-owned by ABRY Partners -- see note on Dallas-Allen record.

reading.body:
The Allentown-TekPark campus publishes 16 MW of IT capacity. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this is roughly 400 racks, or at 8 H100-class accelerators per rack, roughly 3,200 accelerators. The facility opened in 2008 and occupies 58,000 square feet of technical space.

Pennsylvania has 14 mapped data center facilities, of which only 4 publish power capacity. The state's total published capacity is 22.2 MW. This campus ranks fifth among published sites in the state and represents 72 percent of the state's disclosed IT load.

The campus's published operator is listed as TierPoint. The operator's website and current operational status are not published in the available specifications. Verification of ownership is recorded as of September 2026, but no certification status for the facility, grid interconnection details, or power sourcing are published.
